title: High-Hydration Focaccia
description: A gloriously wet, high-hydration focaccia. Bowl-only mixing, no kneading required.

method.instruction: In a large bowl, mix the lukewarm water, instant yeast, and olive oil until the yeast fully dissolves. Congratulations, you've officially started a very wet adventure.

Add the Baker's flour and salt directly into the bowl. Stir with a spatula or your wet hands until everything comes together. The dough will be extremely wet — yes, this is exactly how it should look.

Cover the bowl and let the dough rise until doubled in size (about 2-3 hours at room temperature). During the first hour, perform 1–2 stretch-and-folds using wet hands to help give the dough a little extra structure.
Generously oil your baking tin (approximately 30cm x 40cm). Pour or tip the dough in — no kneading, no bench wrestling required.
Using oiled fingers, gently spread the dough to the edges of the tin, creating dimples all over the surface. Drizzle a bit more olive oil over the top if you like extra richness.
Let rest for 30-45 minutes while you preheat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan-forced).
Just before baking, create more dimples with your fingertips and sprinkle with coarse sea salt and any toppings you like (rosemary, olives, cherry tomatoes).
Bake at 220°C for 20-25 minutes until deeply golden on top and the edges are crisp.
Allow to cool slightly before slicing. Expect a crisp, golden crust and a wonderfully airy, open interior with large, irregular holes.

notes.title: Olive Oil Quality
notes.content: Use the best olive oil you can afford — focaccia absolutely shows the difference. Cobram Classic Extra Virgin Olive Oil works beautifully.

notes.title: The Wet Dough Secret
notes.content: This dough is so wet it's basically a batter. Don't panic! The high hydration creates those beautiful, large air pockets that make artisan-style focaccia so special. Just keep your hands wet when handling it.

notes.title: Best Served
notes.content: Focaccia is best on the day it's baked. Store leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days, then refresh in a warm oven to restore the crust.
